name: Aurora
description: Dual-layer brass and string pad in the style of the two-channel polysynths of the late seventies: notes start dark, speak with a filter overshoot and keep swelling while held.

params.name: Brilliance
params.description: Where the low-pass filters of both layers rest. Lower is dark and muted, like brass played softly; higher is bright and buzzing.

params.name: Low cut
params.description: Where the high-pass filters of both layers sit. Raising it thins the body and leaves a nasal, airy band, the way strings and voices are voiced.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: Emphasis at the corners of both filters. It makes the band between Low cut and Brilliance ring, which turns the tone vocal and horn-like.

params.name: Contour
params.description: How far each note starts below its resting brightness and overshoots above it before settling, the opening of a brass attack. At zero the filter stays still.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a note takes to speak. The level fades in and the contour reaches its brightest point over this time.

params.name: Swell
params.description: How much a held note keeps growing louder and brighter after its attack, as if the key were pressed harder. At zero a held note stays as it is.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to fade after the key is let go. With Contour up, the tone darkens as it fades.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Tuning gap between the two layers, which sets how fast they beat, and how far each voice sits and wanders from the others. At zero everything is in tune.

params.name: Ring
params.description: Amount of a ring modulator sweep at the start of each note: a metallic, bell-like onset that falls in pitch and melts into the pad. At zero there is none.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, grounded in the project's research notes on the Yamaha CS-80 (1977). Modelled in outline: two layers per voice, each through a 12 dB high-pass and then a 12 dB low-pass with resonance; a filter contour that starts below the resting cutoff, overshoots it and settles (the IL/AL envelope); layers detuned against each other with a small fixed tuning offset and a slow drift per voice; a ring modulator whose speed is swept by its own decay. Simplified: the wave is fixed (sawtooth on layer I, sawtooth plus a slowly moving pulse on layer II), one set of knobs serves both layers, and Swell stands in for polyphonic aftertouch by letting level and brightness keep rising while a key is held. Left out: the sine that bypasses the filters, noise, the sub oscillator, the ribbon and the chorus. Choices, not measurements of the original: contour depth (three octaves below, two above), contour decay and release times, the swell time constant (1.6 s) and depth, half keyboard tracking on both filters, layer II voiced a fifth brighter and an octave thinner than layer I, the pulse-width rates, the scatter and drift amounts, the ring sweep (1.4 kHz down to 35 Hz), and a low-pass that opens to 16 kHz at most. The oscillators are band-limited by a four-sample PolyBLEP written for this device (layer_osc.h). It is not a circuit or sample emulation.
